Sci-Fi Industrial Environment Kit
Documentation & User Guide

Thank you for purchasing the Sci-Fi Industrial Environment Kit.

This package contains a collection of modular sci-fi environment assets designed to help you quickly create futuristic industrial facilities, space stations, corridors, hangars, and mechanical environments.

The kit has been created with optimisation and flexibility in mind, using a shared material workflow and a custom shader system that allows you to easily customise the appearance of the entire environment.

Package Contents

The package includes:

101 modular sci-fi environment pieces
Optimised modular meshes
Shared trim sheet material workflow
Custom environment shader
Emissive lighting controls
Panel colour customisation system
Object rotation utility script

All assets are designed to work together seamlessly, allowing you to build large environments while maintaining a clean and efficient material setup.

Modular Asset Workflow

All environment pieces use a shared material system.

Instead of each object having its own unique texture set, the kit uses a single master material that controls the appearance of all assets.

Benefits:

Reduced material count
Improved batching performance
Easy global style changes
Simple colour customisation
Consistent visual appearance across the entire kit

Simply place the modular prefab pieces into your scene and they will automatically use the included material setup.

Custom Sci-Fi Material Shader

The included shader provides creative control over the appearance of the environment.

The material inspector contains several custom parameters:

Surface Inputs
Metallic Intensity

Controls the metallic response of the materials.

Higher values:

More reflective surfaces
More metallic appearance

Lower values:

Less reflective
More painted/plastic appearance
Smoothness Intensity

Controls the surface roughness.

Higher values:

Cleaner polished surfaces
Stronger reflections

Lower values:

Rougher industrial materials
More weathered appearance
Ambient Occlusion Intensity

Controls the strength of the baked ambient occlusion information.

Higher values:

Stronger shadows in creases and panel gaps

Lower values:

Softer surface shading
Lights Intensity

Controls the intensity of emissive lighting effects.

This can be used to adjust how strongly the environment lighting elements appear.

Panel Customisation

The shader includes a dedicated panel masking system.

The included panel mask separates areas of the mesh, allowing you to customise the colour of individual sections without creating additional materials.

Panel Intensity

Controls the brightness/intensity of the masked panel areas.

Increase this value to make panels stand out more.

Panel Colour

Allows you to change the colour of all masked panel sections.

This makes it easy to create variations such as:

Military interiors
Corporate facilities
Alien technology
Warning panels
Different faction styles

Emissive Controls

The shader includes dedicated emissive controls.

You can customise:

Light Colour

Changes the colour of emissive lighting elements.

Examples:

Blue sci-fi lighting
Red warning systems
Green alien technology
Orange industrial lighting
Emissive Intensity

Controls how bright the emissive elements appear.

Higher values:

Strong glowing effects
More intense lighting

Lower values:

Subtle illuminated details
Texture Maps

The material uses the following texture inputs:

Albedo

Controls the base colour information.

Normal

Controls surface detail and small-scale surface depth.

Metallic/Roughness

Controls material response.

Ambient Occlusion

Adds additional depth and shading detail.

Emissive

Controls illuminated areas of the environment.

Included Scripts
Object Spinner

The package includes a simple object rotation script.

This is included for the fan prefab but can be used on any object that requires continuous rotation.

Example uses:

Fans
Machinery
Rotating mechanisms
Display objects
Sci-fi components
Using Object Spinner
Select the object you want to rotate.
Add the:
SpinObject

component.

Adjust:
Rotation Axis

Controls the direction of rotation.

Examples:

X Axis
Y Axis
Z Axis
Rotation Speed

Controls how quickly the object rotates.

Higher values create faster movement.

Showcase Scene

The package includes a fully assembled Showcase Scene, where all 101 modular prefabs are displayed for easy browsing and reference.

This scene demonstrates how the pieces fit together and provides examples of how the modular kit can be combined to create larger environments.

The Showcase Scene also includes demonstrations of the utility scripts included with the package.

Object Spinner Demonstration

A fan assembly in the Showcase Scene demonstrates the SpinObject script in action.

The script can be added to any object that requires continuous rotation, making it useful for animated machinery and environmental props.

The SpinObject component includes the following options:

Play In Editor

When enabled, the object will rotate while editing the scene, allowing you to preview moving objects without entering Play Mode.

When disabled, objects will only rotate during Play Mode.

Rotation Axis

Controls the direction of rotation.

Examples:

X Axis
Y Axis
Z Axis

Rotation Speed

Controls how quickly the object rotates.

Higher values produce faster rotation.

Common uses include:

Cooling fans
Turbines
Mechanical components
Rotating machinery
Display objects
Material Colour Animation Demonstration

The Showcase Scene also includes a demonstration of the Rainbow Material Controller.

This script automatically cycles through colours to showcase the flexibility of the included custom shader.

The demonstration animates both:

Panel Colour
Emissive Light Colour

This provides a quick visual example of how easily the material can be customised to create different themes and colour palettes using a single shared material.

Included Scripts

The package includes two utility scripts.

SpinObject

A simple object rotation component for continuously rotating objects.

Perfect for:

Fans
Machinery
Rotating mechanisms
Display objects
Sci-Fi components

Features

Adjustable Rotation Axis
Adjustable Rotation Speed
Optional Play In Editor mode for previewing movement without entering Play Mode
Rainbow Material Controller

A demonstration script designed to showcase the flexibility of the custom material shader.

The script smoothly cycles through colours over time, updating both the emissive lighting and panel colours simultaneously.

This script is intended as an example of how the shader can be driven through code and can be used as a starting point for creating animated lighting effects, alarms, faction colour changes, or other dynamic material behaviours.

I would also recommend adding a small "Getting Started" section near the beginning of the documentation, as it's something Unity Asset Store buyers often look for:

Getting Started
Import the package into your Unity project.
Open the Showcase Scene to view all included prefabs and example scripts.
Drag the modular prefabs into your own scene to begin building.
Customise the included material using the shader controls to change panel colours, emissive lighting, metallic response, and surface properties.
Add the SpinObject component to any object that requires continuous rotation, or use the included Rainbow Material Controller as an example of runtime material customisation.

This gives new users a clear starting point within the first minute of opening the package.

Recommended Usage

For the best results:

Use the included material as the base material for the kit.
Duplicate the material if you want to create completely different visual themes.
Use the panel colour and emissive controls to create variations.
Combine pieces together to create larger environments.
Performance Notes

The kit has been designed with optimisation in mind.

Recommended practices:

Use baked lighting where possible.
Avoid creating unnecessary material duplicates.
Keep the shared material workflow whenever possible.

Support

If you encounter any issues with the package, please ensure:

You are using a supported Unity version.
The required render pipeline settings are correctly configured.
The included materials and shaders have not been modified incorrectly.

Thank you for supporting this asset pack.

Enjoy building your next sci-fi environment!
